title: Canonical trust policy contract + precedence matrix
description:
Create a canonical trust policy contract consumed by all trust-sensitive surfaces (retrieval, continuity, persona, admin, broadcast safety).

Why:
Without one shared contract, each subsystem can drift in trust/sensitivity interpretation and leak context.

Implementation steps:
1. Define central types and policy helpers:
   - trust levels (`primary|trusted|regular|public`)
   - sensitivity levels (`public|personal|intimate|confidential`)
   - channel visibility classes (`private|semi_private|public|broadcast`)
2. Implement precedence matrix in one place (highest to lowest):
   - explicit operator approval token
   - legal/safety hard block
   - consentFlags gate
   - trust ceiling gate
   - visibility gate
   - scoring/utility preferences
3. Expose a reusable policy API consumed by session manager, memory retrieval, persona overlays, and broadcast send path.
4. Add snapshot tests for policy matrix decisions with expected allow/deny/sanitize outputs.

Files:
- src/trust/policy.ts (new)
- src/trust/types.ts (new)
- src/session/manager.ts
- src/memory/retrieval.ts
- src/agent-loop.ts
- src/channels/* (where visibility is resolved)

Example:
Input: `trust=public`, `memory=confidential`, `consentFlags.allowRecall=false`
Result: deny retrieval regardless of high semantic relevance score.
acceptance_criteria:
- Single trust policy module exists and is imported by retrieval + continuity + prompt/persona composition
- Precedence matrix is explicitly documented in code and tests
- Public/broadcast contexts cannot override consent/trust gates via scoring
- Tests cover at least 12 matrix scenarios across trust/sensitivity/visibility/consent
close_reason: Trust types + policy module created with 39 tests. Types: TrustLevel, SensitivityLevel, ChannelVisibility, ConsentFlags. Policy: evaluateMemoryPolicy (5-layer precedence), classifyChannel, channelsShareContinuity, getAllowedSensitivities.

title: Proper tokenizer — replace chars/4 heuristic with real token counting
description:
Replace the `estimateTokens()` chars/4 heuristic in `src/llm/tokens.ts` with actual tokenizer-based counting. The heuristic is consistently inaccurate — overestimates for English prose, underestimates for code/CJK/structured content. This affects every budget decision: compaction triggers, extraction thresholds, memory retrieval budgets, skill prompt limits.

Current state: `estimateTokens(text)` returns `Math.ceil(text.length / 4)`. Used by:
- `compactionThresholdPct` — triggers auto-compaction in buildContext()
- `extractionThresholdPct` — triggers memory extraction
- `memoryBudgetPct` — limits retrieval token budget
- Skill prompt budget enforcement (planned in PSFN-3oa)
- Runtime context injection (tool directory sizing)

Options for tokenizer library:
- **tiktoken** (OpenAI's BPE tokenizer, WASM) — accurate for GPT models, fast, well-maintained
- **js-tiktoken** — pure JS port, no WASM, slightly slower but zero native deps
- **@anthropic-ai/tokenizer** — if it exists for Claude tokenization
- **gpt-tokenizer** — lightweight alternative

Since we route through LiteLLM to multiple providers (DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi), exact per-model tokenization isn't critical — but BPE-based counting is significantly more accurate than chars/4 for all models. tiktoken with cl100k_base encoding is a good universal approximation.

Features:
- `countTokens(text): number` — real token count
- `countMessageTokens(messages): number` — account for message framing overhead
- Lazy encoder initialization (don't pay startup cost until first call)
- Cache encoding instance (reuse across calls)
- Fallback to chars/4 if tokenizer fails to load
- Replace all `estimateTokens()` callsites
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Tokenizer library added as dependency
- [ ] countTokens(text) with real BPE tokenization
- [ ] countMessageTokens(messages[]) with framing overhead
- [ ] Lazy initialization of encoder (no startup penalty)
- [ ] Graceful fallback to chars/4 on load failure
- [ ] All estimateTokens() callsites migrated
- [ ] Compaction/extraction/memory budget decisions use real counts
- [ ] Tests comparing heuristic vs real counts on sample data
- [ ] Admin dashboard shows real token counts where applicable
close_reason: Completed

title: P1 — Performance Critical Fixes
description:
Five independent performance issues identified across the codebase, ranging from 1-line fixes to moderate wiring changes. Three are HIGH severity (SalienceDecay blocking event loop with 300 individual fsyncs, unbounded SELECT *, sync I/O on every message).

Source: PSFN_META_CODE_22626.md — P1 items #5,#6 (Claude-unique), P2 items #12,#13 (2/3 and 3/3 consensus), #18 (Claude-unique).
design:
All 5 fixes are independent — can be done in any order or parallel:

1. SalienceDecay: wrap decay loop in db.transaction() — 1-line fix, 300 fsyncs → 1
2. Admin memory: add LIMIT/OFFSET to memory listing SELECT — trivial fix
3. embedBatch: pre-embed all texts in MemoryWriter.importBatch() via embedBatch(), use cached embeddings during sequential dedup pass
4. Channel startup: sequential await → Promise.allSettled (prevents one adapter failure from blocking others)
5. writeLastActiveChannel: debounce or make async (currently sync writeFileSync on every incoming message)
acceptance_criteria:
- SalienceDecay runs in single transaction
- Admin memory listing has LIMIT/OFFSET with pagination
- MemoryWriter.importBatch() uses batch embedding (N memories = 1 HTTP call, not N)
- Channel adapters start in parallel via Promise.allSettled
- writeLastActiveChannel doesn't block event loop
- npm run build && npm run test pass
close_reason: Validated complete: all five performance-critical fixes implemented and verified

title: Harden memory retrieval reliability (vector bytes, atomic writes, lexical fallback)
description:
Summary:

- src/memory/retrieval.ts

Implementation steps:
1. Replace unsafe embedding buffer conversion with byteOffset/byteLength-safe serialization/deserialization in memory store paths.
2. Refactor writer supersede and insert flow into an atomic transaction to prevent "superseded but replacement missing" failure windows.
3. Add lexical fallback retrieval path when semantic candidates are empty, with clear provenance markers in results.
4. Improve logging/telemetry for no-candidate causes (threshold, trust filter, embedding mismatch, fallback used).
5. Add regression tests for each failure mode.

After: semantic miss triggers lexical fallback, returning relevant candidates with metadata indicating fallback origin.
acceptance_criteria: Memory retrieval remains functional under semantic misses and write failures, with tests covering serialization, atomicity, and lexical fallback.

title: Default-bind API/Admin to 127.0.0.1 + require auth when port enabled
description: API and Admin HTTP servers bind on all interfaces (0.0.0.0) and auth is optional. If ADMIN_PORT or API_PORT is set without a token/key, anyone on the network can access. 2. `src/channels/admin/server.ts`: Same pattern — add `host` field, default '127.0.0.1'. Log warning if no ADMIN_TOKEN.
3. `src/runtime.ts` + `src/agent-main.ts`: Pass `API_HOST`/`ADMIN_HOST` env vars into server configs.
4. `.env.example`: Add API_HOST and ADMIN_HOST comments.
5. Update tests to use 127.0.0.1 explicitly (they already do in request helpers).
acceptance_criteria:

title: Fix symlink traversal bypass in gateway filesystem policy
description: Gateway filesystem policy uses prefix-based path matching on the normalized (but not canonicalized) path string. A symlink inside the workspace pointing outside it bypasses the ALLOW policy. Fix: resolve paths with `fs.realpathSync` before policy check, reject symlink escapes.
design: In `src/gateway/server.ts` policy evaluation for `fs.read`/`fs.write`: call `fs.realpathSync()` (or `realpath` async) on the requested path, then check the canonical path against policy. If realpath fails (broken symlink), DENY. If canonical path differs from normalized path and falls outside allowed prefixes, DENY.
acceptance_criteria:
- Policy check uses canonical (realpath) path, not raw path
- Symlink pointing outside workspace is DENIED
- Broken symlinks are DENIED
- Normal paths continue to work
- Test with symlink escape scenario
close_reason: realpathSync symlink resolution before policy check. Validated by fresh-eyes reviewer (PASS).

title: Security architecture: containerized agent with tool gateway
description:
The agent runs in a Docker container with NO secrets, NO network egress, and minimal mounts (one RW /workspace). The ONLY way out is a Unix domain socket to a Tool Gateway on the host.

The gateway holds: SecretsManager (in-memory decrypted creds), service proxies (LiteLLM, Discord, Telegram), approval UI/CLI, and an audit log.

This is the foundational security model for everything else — REPL sandbox, sub-agent shards, module system. Nothing else ships until this boundary exists.

Key properties:
- "print process.env" is irrelevant — no secrets in container at all
- No direct internet access — can't exfiltrate via fetch/curl
- Mounts are the filesystem boundary — /workspace RW only
- Approval gating: gateway issues short-lived scoped capability tokens after human approval for anything outside the play area
- isolated-vm becomes guardrails inside the container, not the wall
design:
Architecture:

[Agent container: no secrets, no egress, minimal mounts]
   |  unix domain socket (mounted file)
   v
[Tool Gateway (host)]
   |-- SecretsManager (SOPS+age → in-memory Map)
   |-- LiteLLM proxy (LLM keys)
   |-- Discord narrow API (sendMessage, readChannel — NOT raw HTTP proxy)
   |-- File broker (reads/writes outside /workspace need approval)
   |-- Net broker (POST/PUT to non-allowlisted destinations need approval)
   |-- Approval UI/CLI (human in the loop)
   '-- Audit log (every request logged)

Gateway policy per request: ALLOW / DENY / NEEDS_APPROVAL
- fs.read/write under /workspace → ALLOW
- fs.read/write outside /workspace → NEEDS_APPROVAL
- net.* with request body or non-allowlisted dest → NEEDS_APPROVAL
- discord.sendMessage → ALLOW (within configured channels)
- llm.complete → ALLOW (within budget)

Capability tokens:
- scope = (method, domain/path OR filesystem prefix)
- constraints = (max bytes, TTL, optional one-time use)
- Agent cannot forge — issued by gateway after approval

Container setup:
- docker run --network=none
- Mount: /workspace (RW), /run/gateway.sock (RO)
- No env vars with secrets
- No /home, /etc, /run/secrets mounts

Phases:
1. Container + gateway skeleton (no egress, socket comm, fs.read/write for /workspace)
2. LiteLLM integration behind gateway
3. Discord narrow API behind gateway
4. Approval UI/CLI + capability tokens
5. Audit logging
6. isolated-vm as inner guardrails
acceptance_criteria:
- Agent container has --network=none and no secrets in env/mounts
- Agent can ONLY communicate via Unix socket to gateway
- fs operations outside /workspace are blocked or require approval
- LLM calls route through gateway → LiteLLM, agent never sees API keys
- Discord calls go through narrow typed API, not raw HTTP proxy
- All gateway requests are audit logged
- Approval flow works for privileged operations
notes:
Sprint 4 complete. Core security architecture implemented:

Done:
- Phase 1: Container + gateway skeleton (JSON-RPC 2.0 over NDJSON Unix socket)
- Phase 3: Discord narrow typed API (discord.send, discord.typing, discord.message notification)
- Phase 4 partial: CLI approval flow for privileged ops (y/N prompt)
- Phase 5: Persistent SQLite audit logging (every RPC call with timing + errors)
- Policy engine: workspace ALLOW, outside NEEDS_APPROVAL, unknown DENY
- Content sanitization: 3-layer pipeline (pattern detection → HTML strip → untrusted tagging)
- Docker: Dockerfile.agent + docker-compose.yml with --network=none
- 30 new tests (policy, sanitization, audit)

Remaining (Phase 2 enhancements, not blocking):
- LiteLLM integration (tracked as PSFN-cf3)
- Capability tokens with TTL + scoping
- isolated-vm inner guardrails

6/7 acceptance criteria met. The missing one (LiteLLM) is child issue PSFN-cf3.
close_reason: All 7 acceptance criteria met. Gateway/agent split, Docker --network=none, policy engine, CLI approval, audit logging, content sanitization, LiteLLM proxy (PSFN-cf3), Discord narrow API. Remaining enhancements (capability tokens, isolated-vm) are future work.

title: Tool loop wiring: pass tool schemas to LLM

Fix end-to-end in both single-process and gateway modes:
1. Add `tools` field to `LLMChatParams` in gateway/protocol.ts
2. Convert registered SubstrateTool schemas to pi-ai tool format
3. Pass tools into streamSimple() in LLMClient.stream()
4. Pass tools through GatewayClient.stream() → GatewayServer llm.chat path
5. Include tool list on each iteration of streamWithToolLoop
6. E2E tests for multi-turn tool calling (direct + gateway)
design: Convert SubstrateTool.inputSchema to pi-ai tool format in AgentLoop or LLMClient. The tool list is static per-turn so pass as parameter to stream(). Gateway protocol needs tools array in LLMChatParams.
acceptance_criteria:
- Model consistently emits tool calls when tool-eligible prompts are given
- Same behavior in single-process and gateway/agent split mode
- E2E test covers at least one multi-turn tool call cycle
close_reason: Tool schemas passed through streamWithToolLoop → LLMClient.stream → streamSimple. getToolSchemas() method, LLMContext.tools field, gateway protocol tools field all wired.

title: Add VoiceConnection state monitoring and stale event guards

title: SKILL.md system — markdown-based skill discovery and prompt injection
description:
Adopt OpenClaw's SKILL.md pattern for PSFN. Skills are Markdown files with YAML frontmatter discovered from the filesystem, filtered by eligibility, and injected into the system prompt as structured context. Skills teach the model how to compose existing tools for specific domains — they are NOT executable code.

This replaces PSFN-zfr (module system) with a much simpler, lower-baggage approach that PSFN can self-author via git tools.

Key patterns from OpenClaw:
- `SKILL.md` files with YAML frontmatter (name, description, requires, always)
- Filesystem discovery from multiple dirs with precedence (workspace > managed > bundled)
- Eligibility gating (binary presence, env vars, config flags)
- XML-formatted prompt injection (compact, parseable by model)
- Token budget enforcement (max skills count, max chars)
- Snapshot caching per session (reload on next turn if files change)
- Optional slash-command exposure for user invocation

Integration points:
- Inject into SubstrateAgent.buildRuntimeContext() or as a prompt stack layer
- Skills budget competes with memory/session context (use existing budgeting)
- Git self-modification tools already allow PSFN to author SKILL.md files
- load_tools meta-tool could gain a companion load_skills

Estimated effort: ~800 LoC across 4-5 files
design:
## Architecture

```
src/skills/
  types.ts          — Skill, SkillEntry, SkillMetadata, SkillSnapshot types
  loader.ts         — scanSkillDirs(), loadSkillEntries(), parseSkillFrontmatter()
  filter.ts         — shouldIncludeSkill() eligibility checks
  format.ts         — formatSkillsForPrompt() → XML block
  runtime-wiring.ts — wireSkillsRuntime() bootstrap integration

psfn/skills/ — PSFN's self-authored skills (git-managed)
skills/             — Bundled skills shipped with framework
```

## Skill Format
```markdown
---
name: memory-management
description: "Query, write, and manage L2 memories"
metadata:
  always: true
---
# Memory Management
## When to Use
When you need to search, write, or manage memories...
## Tools Available
- memory_write: Create new memories
- memory_search (via think tool): Query memory store
```

## Loading Precedence (highest wins)
1. `psfn/skills/` (self-authored, git-tracked)
2. `skills/` (bundled with framework)
3. Config `skills.extraDirs[]` if any

## Prompt Injection
Compact XML block injected into runtime context:
```xml
<skills>
  <skill name="memory-management" path="psfn/skills/memory-management/SKILL.md">
    Query, write, and manage L2 memories
  </skill>
  ...
</skills>
```
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Skill type definitions with YAML frontmatter parsing
- [ ] Filesystem discovery from multiple directories with precedence
- [ ] Eligibility filtering (binary, env, config checks)
- [ ] XML prompt formatting with token budget limits

- [ ] Wired into SubstrateAgent runtime context

- [ ] Admin UI "Skills" page showing loaded/filtered skills
- [ ] Tests for loader, filter, formatter
- [ ] Settings in skills.json (dirs, limits, enabled/disabled per skill)

title: API: prevent stranded in-flight turns (timeout/disconnect handling)
description:
Summary: API chat completions can leave the agent in a long-running in-flight state after client timeout, causing subsequent requests to fail with `Agent is already processing a prompt` and return 500s. Add request lifecycle controls so timeout/disconnect does not strand the channel.

2. Add request timeout handling for non-streaming requests (configurable via env, with sensible default) and detect client disconnect (`req.aborted` / `res.close`) to stop waiting.
3. Propagate cancellation signal where supported; otherwise ensure API returns deterministic timeout/busy errors and clears server-side bookkeeping safely.
4. Return explicit 429/503-style busy response instead of generic 500 for channel-busy contention.
5. Add regression tests for: timeout path, disconnect path, in-flight contention behavior, and successful recovery after timeout.

Example:
Before: Request A times out at client, request B on same `X-Session-ID` -> 500 internal error (`already processing`).
After: Request A yields timeout/busy response and bookkeeping cleanup; request B either queues/returns busy deterministically and succeeds once channel is free.

title: Restore global latest session by timestamp across restart (Discord-primary)
description:
Summary:
Implement global default session resumption across restart by restoring the most recent session (latest message timestamp) across all channels, with Discord as the primary live chat surface.

Clarified requirement:
- Scope is NOT Garden-only state restoration.
- On restart, runtime/session-aware surfaces should default to the latest session by timestamp.
- Discord continuity must remain first-class (Discord is primary UI), while still supporting cross-channel session sources.

Validated current behavior:
- Discord turns are keyed by channel-derived session IDs, so continuity exists when a new message arrives on that same channel.
- There is no explicit global “active session” restore path that selects the latest session by timestamp at startup for default runtime/session context.
- Garden-specific identity defaults are a separate concern and should not define global session semantics.

Files to modify:
- src/session/store.ts
- src/session/manager.ts
- src/lifecycle/notifications.ts
- src/agent-main.ts
- src/runtime.ts
- src/channels/admin/chat/bootstrap.ts (only where it should consume global default, not redefine it)
- tests:
  - src/session/store.test.ts
  - src/lifecycle/notifications.test.ts
  - targeted runtime/admin bootstrap tests

Implementation steps:
1. Add a canonical resolver for “latest session” by last entry timestamp across channels.
2. Persist global last-active-session metadata (session id + timestamp + channel type) on message activity.
3. Restore that metadata on startup; if missing/stale, fall back to computed latest-by-timestamp session.
4. Thread this global default into startup/session-aware entrypoints while preserving Discord per-channel continuity semantics.
5. Add restart-focused tests covering multi-channel ordering and fallback behavior.

Example (before -> after):
- Before: restart does not explicitly restore global latest session context.
- After: restart defaults to the most recent session ID/timestamp, with Discord-primary flows continuing naturally.

title: P2 — DRY Utility Extraction
description:
17 distinct duplication patterns identified across the codebase: parsePositiveIntEnv (5 copies), isRecord (5+ files), toErrorMessage pattern (78 occurrences), hasColumn (2 copies), DB pragma init (8 locations), JSONL append (6 implementations), atomic file write (4 inline), registerTool interface (7+ declarations), body-parsers (admin+API), SQLite transaction wrappers, and more.

title: SillyTavern-style prompt manager + macro variables for system prompt composition
description:
Summary:
Implement a Prompt Manager flow inspired by SillyTavern's setupChatCompletionPromptManager() for PSFN prompt composition, with first-class macro/variable interpolation so prompt templates can reference runtime data safely.

Why:
Current prompt stack is layer-based but lacks prompt-manager semantics (required prompt sections, stable ordering, and robust missing-entry handling). It also freezes {{user}} to a static value during seed/compose, causing identity mismatch in conversational output.

Files to modify:
- src/identity/prompt-manager.ts (new)
- src/identity/prompt-manager.test.ts (new)
- src/identity/prompt-runtime.ts
- src/identity/loader.ts
- src/identity/prompt-composer.ts

- src/runtime.ts
- src/agent-main.ts
- src/channels/admin/templates/prompts.ts (if prompt-manager metadata is surfaced)
- src/channels/admin/server.test.ts and/or identity prompt tests

Implementation steps:
1. Add a Prompt Manager primitive that guarantees required named prompt entries exist and are composed in deterministic order.
2. Keep compatibility with current layer storage while introducing prompt-entry metadata (identifier, role, enabled, order/priority, marker-like behavior if needed).
3. Add macro interpolation for prompt templates with {{user}} and {{char}} baseline support plus additional runtime variables (channel, trust, model, date/time, canonical contact id).
4. Ensure interpolation runs per-turn using runtime author context (not one-time at startup), while preserving existing date/time runtime token behavior.
5. Stop freezing {{user}} to a static fallback during initial character card composition/seeding.
6. Add tests for required-entry auto-heal behavior, ordering, and macro expansion correctness/fallback behavior.
7. Validate no regressions in extraction/compaction/static prompt registry flows.

Example:
Before -> base prompt contains literal "User" from startup substitution; runtime context separately knows actual author name.
After -> base template can keep {{user}} and resolves per turn to current author (e.g., Operator) while {{char}} resolves to character name (e.g., PSFN), plus additional runtime variables for advanced templates.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Prompt Manager module exists and is wired for system prompt composition
- [ ] Required prompt entries are auto-healed when missing
- [ ] Deterministic prompt ordering is enforced
- [ ] Macro interpolation supports {{user}} and {{char}}
- [ ] Additional runtime macros are supported (channel/model/trust/date-time identifiers)
- [ ] {{user}} is no longer permanently frozen to startup fallback value
- [ ] Unit tests cover prompt manager behavior and macro interpolation
- [ ] Existing prompt-related tests pass

title: Harden session channelId filename sanitization
description: SessionStore.sanitizeChannelId only replaces `/` and `:`. Channel IDs with other path-metacharacters (null bytes, `..`, backslashes, control chars) could produce unsafe or ambiguous filenames. Fix: restrict to strict allowlist `[a-zA-Z0-9._-]` and hex-encode everything else.
design: Replace current `sanitizeChannelId` with: keep `[a-zA-Z0-9._-]` as-is, replace everything else with `%XX` hex encoding (like URL encoding but for filenames). This is lossless — `listChannels()` can reverse it. Update `listChannels()` to use the reverse decode instead of reading first JSONL line (more efficient).
acceptance_criteria:

- listChannels can reverse the encoding losslessly

title: Fix streaming chunk cross-talk: per-request IDs in gateway LLM proxy
description: Gateway emits `llm.chunk` with constant `requestId: 0`. Client keeps a single global handler. Under concurrent shard LLM streams, chunks can leak between tasks. Fix: generate unique request IDs per stream call, route chunk handlers by request ID on both gateway server and client sides.
design:
1. Gateway server (`src/gateway/server.ts`): generate a unique requestId (incrementing counter or UUID) per `llm.stream` call. Pass it in every `llm.chunk` notification.
2. Gateway client (`src/gateway/client.ts`): replace single global `onChunkHandler` with a `Map<string, handler>` keyed by requestId. Register handler before sending `llm.stream`, remove on completion/error.
3. Protocol (`src/gateway/protocol.ts`): update `LLMChunkNotification` type to use `string` requestId instead of hardcoded `0`.
4. Ensure backward compat: if requestId is missing/0, fall back to global handler (graceful degradation).
acceptance_criteria:
- Concurrent shard LLM streams route chunks to correct handlers
- Existing single-stream usage still works
- Gateway protocol types updated
- Tests verify concurrent stream isolation
close_reason: Per-request streaming IDs with Map-based handler dispatch. Validated by fresh-eyes reviewer (PASS).

title: Scope-aware cross-channel continuity
description:
Currently each Discord channel (including DMs) gets a separate JSONL session. Moving between channels loses short-term context. Need a hybrid continuity model:

1. Keep per-channel transcript storage (audit/source truth stays channel-scoped)
2. Add per-user continuity thread for short-term context carryover
3. Build prompt from both: recent channel messages (local) + recent user continuity messages (cross-channel)
4. Channel metadata: visibility = private | semi_private | public | broadcast
5. Source metadata per message: source_channel_id, source_channel_type, source_visibility
6. At prompt-build time: always include local channel context, include user-thread filtered by target visibility
7. Visibility policy: private target (DM) can use all; public target (guild) only public + sanitized private summary; broadcast target (tweet) public-only unless explicit approval

Phase 1 (now): Full user continuity for "just us" — all messages visible across channels.
Phase 2 (later): Scope filtering when more public channels exist.
design: Add ChannelMetadata type with visibility field. Add UserContinuityStore that indexes recent messages by userId across channels. SessionManager.buildContext() merges local entries + user continuity entries. Phase 1: no visibility filtering. Phase 2: add scope-based filtering at prompt-build time.
acceptance_criteria:
- Messages in DM are visible as context when chatting in guild channel and vice versa
- Each message stores origin channel + visibility metadata
- Prompt builder merges local channel + user continuity thread
- No regression on per-channel JSONL storage (audit trail intact)
close_reason: UserContinuityStore (per-user JSONL), SessionEntry.originChannelId, manager wiring, 17 tests passing. Cross-channel messages injected into system prompt via buildContext userId param.

description:
Summary:

- applySettings() updates config.primaryModel / config.extractionModel but does not synchronize config.modelRoster slots (chat, background).

3. Ensure admin settings update path invokes the refresh hook after saving/applying settings.
4. Add tests proving model/provider/token changes in settings are reflected in actual resolved model IDs for subsequent turns.

Example:

After: next turn resolves and uses moonshotai/kimi-k2.5 immediately.

title: Wire embedBatch() into MemoryWriter.importBatch()
description:
MemoryWriter.importBatch() at writer.ts:752-761 processes records sequentially, calling this.write() for each (which calls embed() individually). For N memories, this makes N separate HTTP roundtrips to Ollama.

embedBatch() exists on EmbeddingService and works (used by migration.ts) — it sends all texts in one HTTP POST.

title: RLM evidence/provenance tracking in ThinkResult
description:
PSFN's ThinkResult returns only aggregate stats (iterations, token counts, duration). There's no record of what the think tool actually searched, found, or concluded at each step. This makes it impossible to cite sources, debug reasoning, or generate reflection memories about how conclusions were reached.

Aleph (github.com/Hmbown/aleph) tracks an evidence trail — every search, sub-LM call, and code execution records a citation with source, snippet, and timestamp.
design:
## Pattern (from Aleph `aleph/mcp/session.py:78-130`)

```python
@dataclass
class _Evidence:
    source: str  # "search", "peek", "exec", "manual", "sub_query"
    line_range: tuple[int, int] | None
    pattern: str | None
    snippet: str
    note: str | None = None
    timestamp: datetime
```

Session also tracks convergence: `confidence_history: list[float]`, `information_gain: list[int]`.

## PSFN Design

### New types in `src/repl/types.ts`

```typescript
export interface ThinkEvidence {
  source: 'memory_search' | 'memory_get' | 'session_messages' | 'llm_query' | 'code';
  query?: string;         // search query or llm prompt (truncated)
  snippet: string;        // what was found (truncated to ~200 chars)
  resultCount?: number;   // how many results returned
  timestamp: number;
}

export interface ThinkStep {
  iteration: number;
  code: string;            // code the LLM wrote (truncated)
  output: string;          // execution output (truncated)
  error: string | null;
  evidenceCollected: ThinkEvidence[];
  tokensUsed: number;      // this iteration's token count
}
```

### Changes

1. `src/repl/types.ts` — Add `ThinkEvidence`, `ThinkStep`. Extend `ThinkResult` with:
   ```typescript
   steps: ThinkStep[];
   evidence: ThinkEvidence[];  // flattened from all steps
   ```

2. `src/repl/sandbox.ts` — Add evidence collection hooks to injected functions:
   - `memory_search`: record query, result count, top result snippet
   - `memory_get_by_id`: record id, text snippet
   - `session_messages`: record channelId, message count
   - `llm_query`: record prompt (first 100 chars), response (first 200 chars)
   
   Evidence array lives on sandbox instance, collected per-execution:
   ```typescript
   private currentEvidence: ThinkEvidence[] = [];
   
   // In memory_search:
   this.currentEvidence.push({
     source: 'memory_search',
     query,
     snippet: results[0]?.text.slice(0, 200) ?? '',
     resultCount: results.length,
     timestamp: Date.now(),
   });
   ```
   
   Add `collectEvidence(): ThinkEvidence[]` method that drains and returns.

3. `src/repl/loop.ts` — After each sandbox.execute():
   - Collect evidence via `sandbox.collectEvidence()`
   - Build `ThinkStep` with code, output, error, evidence, tokens
   - Push to `steps[]` array
   - At end: flatten all step evidence into top-level `evidence[]`

4. `src/repl/tools.ts` — Include evidence summary in tool output:
   ```
   [Think: 5 iters, 8420 tokens, 1200ms, 12 evidence items]
   ```

### Use cases
- PSFN can cite: "Based on 3 memories I found about X..."
- Admin GUI can show reasoning chains in Active Branches
- Reflection memories can reference what evidence informed a conclusion
acceptance_criteria:
- ThinkEvidence and ThinkStep types defined
- memory_search, memory_get_by_id, session_messages, llm_query all record evidence
- ThinkResult includes steps[] and evidence[] arrays
- Think tool output header shows evidence count
- Evidence snippets truncated to prevent bloat

title: Model fallback chains — wire roster routing with error-classified retry
description:
Replace the dead-code ModelSlot/ModelPurpose/resolveModelSlot() system with actual primary+fallbacks routing inspired by OpenClaw's model-fallback.ts pattern.

Current state: resolveModelSlot() exists with fallback chains (background→chat, reasoning→chat, longContext→chat), ModelPurpose has 4 variants, settings form has 4 roster slots — but SubstrateAgent.handleMessage() and LLMClient.stream() always hard-select config.primaryModel/config.primaryProvider. Nothing routes through the roster.

OpenClaw pattern to adopt:
- Primary model + ordered fallbacks[] per purpose
- Error classification: timeout, context overflow, rate limit, auth, billing → determines retry vs. rethrow
- Sequential fallback: try candidates in order, track attempts
- Cooldown tracking: rate-limited providers get temporary cooldown, probe to detect recovery
- Per-purpose model config: chat (primary), background (extraction/compaction), reasoning (think tool)
- Model allowlist filtering

Key difference from OpenClaw: we route through LiteLLM proxy, so provider auth rotation isn't needed — but model fallback on error classification IS valuable.

Config source: models.json (not hardcoded in types.ts)
design:
## Config (data/models.json)
```json
{
  "chat": {
    "primary": "deepseek/deepseek-v3.2",
    "fallbacks": ["z-ai/glm-5", "moonshotai/kimi-k2.5"]
  },
  "background": {
    "primary": "deepseek/deepseek-v3.2",
    "fallbacks": []
  },
  "reasoning": {
    "primary": "moonshotai/kimi-k2.5",
    "fallbacks": ["deepseek/deepseek-v3.2"]
  }
}
```

## Error Classification (src/llm/error-classify.ts)
- ABORT → never retry (user cancelled)
- CONTEXT_OVERFLOW → never retry (would fail worse)
- RATE_LIMIT → retry with cooldown
- TIMEOUT → retry next candidate
- AUTH → retry next candidate
- UNKNOWN → retry next candidate

## Fallback Runner (src/llm/fallback.ts)
```typescript
async function runWithFallback<T>(
  purpose: ModelPurpose,
  config: ModelsConfig,
  run: (model: string, provider: string) => Promise<T>
): Promise<{ result: T; model: string; attempts: number }>
```

## Integration Points
- LLMClient.stream() calls runWithFallback() instead of hard-selecting primary
- SubstrateAgent.handleMessage() passes purpose='chat'
- Think tool REPL passes purpose='reasoning'
- Extraction/compaction passes purpose='background'
- Admin settings form reads/writes models.json
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] models.json as source of truth for model routing config
- [ ] Error classification module (timeout, overflow, rate limit, auth, abort)
- [ ] runWithFallback() with sequential candidate trying + attempt tracking
- [ ] Cooldown tracking for rate-limited models
- [ ] LLMClient.stream()/complete() wired through fallback runner
- [ ] Purpose-based routing (chat, background, reasoning) actually used
- [ ] Admin settings reads/writes models.json
- [ ] Logging: which model was selected, why fallback occurred
- [ ] Tests for error classification and fallback sequencing

title: Pluggable embedding providers (transformers.js, Ollama, API)
description:

2. **transformers.js** (@huggingface/transformers) — in-process ONNX inference, zero network overhead, fastest for local use on 48-core Threadripper
3. **API-based** — OpenAI, Cohere, or any OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings endpoint

The EmbeddingService interface already exists (embed + embedBatch + dims). Each provider implements it. Selection via EMBEDDING_PROVIDER env var (ollama|transformers|api) with provider-specific config (model, URL, API key, etc.).

transformers.js is the speed win — eliminates HTTP overhead entirely for local embedding. Especially impactful when combined with the embedBatch() wiring from PSFN-72ez.

Low priority add-on to the performance epic — nice-to-have after batch embedding is wired.
design:
1. Define EmbeddingProviderFactory pattern: createEmbeddingProvider(config) returns EmbeddingService
2. OllamaEmbeddingProvider (existing, refactored)
3. TransformersEmbeddingProvider — @huggingface/transformers with pipeline('feature-extraction', model), Float32Array output, auto-download model on first use
4. ApiEmbeddingProvider — fetch to /v1/embeddings (OpenAI-compatible)
5. Config: EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=ollama|transformers|api, EMBEDDING_MODEL, EMBEDDING_DIMS, EMBEDDING_API_URL, EMBEDDING_API_KEY
6. Default stays Ollama for backward compat
acceptance_criteria:
- All 3 providers implement EmbeddingService (embed + embedBatch + dims)
- EMBEDDING_PROVIDER env var selects provider
- transformers.js runs fully in-process (no HTTP)
- Existing Ollama path unchanged as default

Implementation steps:

2. On shutdown, stop new extraction triggers and await drain with bounded timeout.
3. Close DB only after extraction drain completes or timeout is logged.
4. Add tests simulating shutdown during extraction.

Example:
Before: stop -> scheduler stops, DB closes, then extractor callback throws database closed errors.
After: stop waits for extraction drain and shuts down cleanly.

title: Discord trigger words, reaction triggers, and listening windows

- **Reaction triggers**: React with a configured emoji (default `👆`) on any message to invoke the bot on it. React `❌` on bot's own message to delete it.
- **Listening windows**: After a trigger fires, keep listening to that user in that channel for a configurable duration (default 2 min) so follow-ups flow naturally. `!i` prefix opts out.
- **Runtime-editable**: All trigger settings (words, reactions, window duration) are editable via admin Settings page — no restart needed.

Credit: `Co-Authored-By: darkacorn <darkacorn@users.noreply.github.com>` in final commit. Close PR #2 with a comment linking to our implementation.

Key constraints:
- No hardcoded bot IDs, paths, or names
- Keep `pendingByChannel` gateway-mode queue intact

- Scope all behavior changes to `src/channels/discord/adapter.ts`

title: Add SSRF defenses to gateway web.fetch
description: Gateway `web.fetch` allows arbitrary URLs without domain filtering. A prompt-injected agent could probe localhost, private networks, cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254), etc. Fix: enforce URL policy — deny private/link-local/localhost CIDRs, require HTTPS by default, optional domain allowlist.
design:
1. Add `isPrivateUrl(url)` utility in `src/gateway/server.ts` (or a new `src/gateway/url-policy.ts`): parse URL, resolve hostname to IP via `dns.lookup`, check against RFC1918/link-local/loopback/metadata CIDRs.
2. In `web.fetch` handler: validate URL before fetching. Deny private targets. Deny non-HTTPS unless explicitly configured (`ALLOW_HTTP_FETCH=true`).
3. Optional `FETCH_DOMAIN_ALLOWLIST` env var — comma-separated domains. If set, only those domains are allowed.
4. Return policy denial as RPC error, not silent failure.
acceptance_criteria:
- localhost/127.0.0.1/::1 URLs are DENIED
- Private CIDR (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x) targets DENIED
- Link-local (169.254.x) DENIED (blocks cloud metadata)
- HTTP denied by default (HTTPS required)
- Domain allowlist works when configured
- Normal HTTPS URLs continue to work
- Tests cover all denial cases

title: Partial frozen system prompt for prefix cache
description:
Split system prompt into static (~1/3) and dynamic (~2/3) portions. Freeze static portion at session start for LLM prefix cache optimization.

Design:
- Split composed prompt into two sections:
  - STATIC (frozen at session start): base layer (personality, character card), operator layer, channel-specific static instructions
  - DYNAMIC (rebuilt per-turn): runtime context (time, channel, trust, model), memory retrieval results, persona adaptation, tool directory, scratchpad
- Cache static portion hash; only recompose when layers actually change (toggle/update via prompt tools)
- Place static content FIRST in system prompt so LLM prefix cache covers it
- PromptComposer.compose() returns { static: string, dynamic: string } or composes with a stable prefix

Hermes reference: /tools/memory_tool.py (_system_prompt_snapshot pattern)

Acceptance:
- [ ] System prompt split into static prefix + dynamic suffix
- [ ] Static portion frozen at session start
- [ ] Dynamic portion rebuilt per-turn as today
- [ ] Static cache invalidated when prompt layers are edited
- [ ] Measurable prefix cache hit improvement (test with Claude/API that reports cache stats)
- [ ] No behavioral regression

title: A3: Crash recovery extraction
description:
If the process crashes between extraction intervals, everything since the last extraction exists only in L0 JSONL. On restart, the session loads but L2 extraction doesn't retroactively run on recovered entries. The companion has raw history but not distilled memories.

Source: Lobstar incident analysis

Files: src/session/store.ts, src/memory/extraction.ts, src/runtime.ts

- On startup, detect unclean shutdown (absence of graceful shutdown marker in last JSONL entry)
- If unclean: identify un-extracted session entries (entries after last extraction marker)
- Queue retroactive extraction for those entries
- Write extraction marker to JSONL after each successful extraction run

Acceptance:
- [ ] Graceful shutdown marker written to active sessions on clean stop
- [ ] Unclean shutdown detected on startup
- [ ] Un-extracted entries identified via extraction markers
- [ ] Retroactive extraction queued on unclean recovery
- [ ] Test: kill process mid-conversation, restart, verify L2 memories extracted from pre-crash entries

title: B1: Cryptographic session integrity (HMAC)
description:
Session JSONL files are plain text. If anyone gains filesystem access (or the companion edits her own sessions via REPL), fabricated entries are indistinguishable from real ones. The model trusts its own history blindly.

Source: 0din "Your AI Agent Has a Memory Problem" research

Files: src/session/journal-utils.ts, src/session/store.ts, src/gateway/server.ts

Work:
- Each JSONL entry gets an HMAC-SHA256 using a gateway-held signing key
- HMAC field appended to each JSON line: { ...entry, _hmac: "..." }
- On session load, verify the HMAC chain — any line that fails verification gets flagged
- Failed entries wrapped in <unverified_history> tags (reuse existing sanitization pattern)
- Agent-side code never has access to the signing key (gateway-only secret)
- Signing key rotation: support key versioning, old HMACs still verifiable with old keys

Acceptance:
- [ ] HMAC-SHA256 on every JSONL entry
- [ ] Signing key held by gateway only
- [ ] Failed verification entries tagged <unverified_history>
- [ ] Key rotation with version support
- [ ] Test: modify entry, verify unverified tag on load
- [ ] Test: unmodified entries pass verification
close_reason: Wired integrity provider into single-process runtime.ts via env var keyring resolution. 5 new tests verify round-trip signing, tamper detection, and backward compat with no keyring. Split mode already worked.

title: Trust-Gated Memory & Channel Visibility (Honne/Tatemae)
description:
Implement trust-based memory privacy, contact relationship tracking, and channel visibility policy so PSFN can maintain appropriate boundaries across different social contexts.

Core principle: Honne (true self, full memories) vs Tatemae (public face, filtered sharing). PSFN knows everything but only shares what's appropriate for who she's talking to.

Two orthogonal dimensions:
1. Contact Trust Level: primary > trusted > regular > public
2. Memory Sensitivity: public > personal > intimate > confidential

Prior design work: Anthropic conversation e2b32e80 (Feb 2025), multiple ChatGPT discussions. See research reports from 2026-02-14 session.
design:
## Architecture

### New: Contacts Table (SQLite)
- id, discordUserId, displayName, trustLevel, relationshipType
- emotionalBaseline (JSON), firstSeen, lastSeen, notes
- PSFN maintains this via tools and extraction

### Modified: L2 Memories
- Add `sensitivity` column: public|personal|intimate|confidential
- Add `consentFlags` column: JSON (opt-in recall, deletion consent, abstraction-allowed)
- Tagged during extraction by updated extraction prompt
- MemoryRetriever hard-filters by channel trust ceiling
- Sensitive memories also get continuous `privacy_risk` penalty in scoring (not just binary gate)
- Higher salience threshold required to STORE sensitive content in the first place

### Modified: Continuity Store
- channelVisibility enforced in getRecent()
- Channel → trust mapping (DM=primary, group=regular, public=public)
- Primary channels share full continuity (DM + OpenWebUI + SillyTavern = one thread)

### Modified: Agent Loop
- Per-trust persona system prompt injection (honne vs tatemae)
- Response filter pass for lower-trust contexts (future)

### New: 6th Memory Type — relational
- Facts about people and relationships
- "V's sister is [name]", "Bob likes jazz"
- contactId foreign key links to contacts table

### New Concepts from ChatGPT Research
1. Continuous privacy_risk penalty in scoring formula (not just binary gate)
2. "Forget but keep the lesson" — abstract sensitive memories instead of delete
3. Mode-based retrieval presets (work/comfort/reflection/minimal) orthogonal to trust
4. Anti-reinforcement guardrail: privacy classification trumps utility scoring, always
5. Namespace isolation: deny-cross-namespace by default (personal/work/shared)
6. Per-memory consent flags and access policy as first-class fields

title: RLM trajectory logging (per-step breakdown in ThinkResult)
description:
PSFN's ThinkResult has aggregate stats but no per-iteration breakdown. There's no way to inspect what code ran at each step, what output it produced, or how tokens were distributed across iterations. This makes debugging multi-step reasoning opaque.

Aleph (github.com/Hmbown/aleph) logs every iteration as a `TrajectoryStep` with timing, tokens, code, and result.
design:
## Pattern (from Aleph `aleph/types.py:99-117`) ```python @dataclass class TrajectoryStep: step_number: int depth: int timestamp: datetime prompt_tokens: int prompt_summary: str # first 500 chars action: ParsedAction result: ExecutionResult result_tokens: int cumulative_tokens: int cumulative_cost: float ``` ## PSFN Design This overlaps with the evidence tracking issue (PSFN-xxx) — the `ThinkStep` type defined there already captures code, output, error, evidence, and tokens per iteration. This issue focuses on the **admin GUI visualization** and **extended metadata**. ### Additional fields on ThinkStep ```typescript export interface ThinkStep { iteration: number; timestamp: number; code: string; // LLM-generated code (full, not truncated for logging) output: string; // execution output error: string | null; evidenceCollected: ThinkEvidence[]; inputTokens: number; // LLM prompt tokens this iteration outputTokens: number; // LLM response tokens this iteration cumulativeTokens: number; // running total durationMs: number; // wall time for this iteration (LLM + execution) variablesChanged: string[]; // which sandbox vars were created/modified } ``` ### Admin GUI integration `src/channels/admin/templates.ts` — Add a "Reasoning Traces" section (or extend Active Branches) that renders ThinkStep arrays as a timeline: ```html
#1 120 in / 85 out 340ms 
const results = await memory_search("V's preferences");
Found 3 results...
``` ### Variable tracking (from Aleph `aleph/repl/sandbox.py:766-793`) Before/after each `execute()`, diff the sandbox context: ```typescript // In REPLSandbox: getVariablesDiff(): string[] { const current = new Set(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(this.context)); const changed = [...current].filter(k => !this.previousKeys.has(k) || this.context[k] !== this.previousValues.get(k)); this.previousKeys = current; this.previousValues = new Map([...current].map(k => [k, this.context[k]])); return changed.filter(k => !builtinKeys.has(k)); } ``` Report `variablesChanged` back to the LLM in the iteration feedback: ``` [Iteration 3 | 205 tokens | vars changed: results, summary] ```
acceptance_criteria:
- ThinkStep includes per-iteration timing, tokens, cumulative totals
- Variable change tracking reports which sandbox vars were created/modified
- Iteration feedback to LLM includes variable change summary
- ThinkResult.steps[] available for admin GUI rendering
- Admin GUI has basic trajectory view for think results
notes: Variable tracking (acceptance criteria 4+5) already implemented by PSFN-ylj: `ExecuteResult.variablesChanged` exists, loop.ts feeds it back as "Variables changed: ..." in iteration feedback. Remaining work: ThinkStep type, per-iteration timing/tokens/cumulative fields, admin GUI timeline view, and wiring steps[] into ThinkResult.
close_reason: Extended ThinkStep with timestamp/input/output/cumulative/duration/variables; loop now records per-iteration trajectory metadata and richer feedback. Added agent.think.trace event, admin trace capture, dashboard Reasoning Traces view, and tests.

title: RLM REPL text analysis helpers (search, grep, diff, group_by)
description:
PSFN's REPL sandbox has 13 injected functions, all focused on memory/session/LLM access. There are no text analysis utilities. PSFN can search memories but can't grep through results, diff two memories, or frequency-analyze conversation patterns without writing raw JS each time.

Aleph has 100+ helpers. We don't need all of them — cherry-pick the ones relevant to introspection over memories and conversations.
design:
## Cherry-picked helpers (from Aleph `aleph/repl/helpers.py`)

Port these ~12 functions as lightweight JS implementations in a new `src/repl/helpers.ts`:

### Text search
```typescript
// Regex search with context lines (like grep -C)
function search(text: string, pattern: string, contextLines?: number): string[]

// Line filtering
function grep(text: string, pattern: string): string       // matching lines
function grep_v(text: string, pattern: string): string      // non-matching lines
```

### Text extraction
```typescript
// Extract text between markers
function between(text: string, start: string, end: string): string

// First N / last N lines
function head(text: string, n?: number): string
function tail(text: string, n?: number): string
```

### Analysis
```typescript
// Word frequency map
function word_frequency(text: string): Record<string, number>

// Simple line diff (added/removed)
function diff(a: string, b: string): string
```

### Collections (operate on arrays from memory_search results)
```typescript
// Deduplicate by key
function dedupe<T>(arr: T[], key: (item: T) => string): T[]

// Group by key
function group_by<T>(arr: T[], key: (item: T) => string): Record<string, T[]>

// Partition by predicate
function partition<T>(arr: T[], pred: (item: T) => boolean): [T[], T[]]
```

### Similarity
```typescript
// Jaccard similarity between two texts (word-level)
function text_similarity(a: string, b: string): number
```

## Implementation

1. `src/repl/helpers.ts` (new, ~150 lines) — Pure functions, no deps.

2. `src/repl/sandbox.ts` — Import and inject all helpers into vm context. Add to builtinKeys set.

3. `src/repl/helpers.test.ts` (new) — Unit tests for each helper.

## NOT porting (document analysis, not introspection)
- extract_emails, extract_urls, extract_dates, extract_functions, extract_classes, extract_imports
- chunk(), cite(), embed_text(), semantic_search() (we have memory_search)
- is_valid_json, is_valid_email, is_valid_url
- columns(), sort_lines(), uniq() (trivial in JS)
- ngrams() (academic, not practical for PSFN)
acceptance_criteria:
- ~12 text analysis helpers available in REPL sandbox
- search/grep/grep_v work with regex patterns
- word_frequency, diff, text_similarity work on strings
- dedupe/group_by/partition work on arrays
- All helpers are pure functions with no external deps
- Unit tests for each helper
close_reason: 12 text analysis helpers implemented + 43 tests. Merged from wt/repl-helpers.

title: Config externalization — JSON files as source of truth, not hardcoded defaults
description:
Move all hardcoded configuration defaults out of TypeScript source files into JSON config files under data/. This enables backup, migration, and editing without code changes.

Current state: SubstrateConfig in types.ts has ~40 fields with hardcoded defaults parsed from env vars. settings.ts has SETTINGS_VALIDATION with hardcoded ranges. Model defaults are in types.ts. Scheduler intervals, memory thresholds, trust ceilings — all baked into code.

Target state: JSON files under data/ are the source of truth. TypeScript types define the schema and provide validation, but defaults come from JSON seed files that ship with the repo. Runtime loads JSON → validates → merges with env overrides.

Files to externalize:
- data/settings.json (already exists, expand to cover all settings)
- data/models.json (new — model roster, fallbacks, aliases)
- data/skills.json (new — skill dirs, limits, per-skill enable/disable)
- data/scheduler.json (new — task definitions, intervals, maintenance config)
- data/trust-policy.json (new — trust ceilings, sensitivity defaults, channel visibility rules)

Pattern: JSON file → Zod/TypeBox validation → typed config object → runtime reads per-call. Atomic writes via tmp+rename (already used for settings.json). Seed files in repo root for first-run bootstrap.
design:
## Directory Structure
```
data/                          — runtime data (gitignored)
  settings.json                — editable settings (exists, expand)
  models.json                  — model roster + fallbacks
  skills.json                  — skill loader config
  scheduler.json               — scheduler task definitions
  trust-policy.json            — trust/privacy policy config
  heartbeat-policy.json        — already exists via HeartbeatPolicyStore

config/                        — seed files (checked into repo)
  settings.seed.json           — default settings for first run
  models.seed.json             — default model config
  skills.seed.json             — default skill config
  scheduler.seed.json          — default scheduler config
  trust-policy.seed.json       — default trust policy
```

## Bootstrap Pattern
```typescript
function loadOrSeed<T>(dataPath: string, seedPath: string, validate: (v: unknown) => T): T {
  if (existsSync(dataPath)) return validate(JSON.parse(readFileSync(dataPath)));
  const seed = validate(JSON.parse(readFileSync(seedPath)));
  writeAtomicSync(dataPath, JSON.stringify(seed, null, 2));
  return seed;
}
```

## Migration
- Existing hardcoded defaults become seed file values
- Env vars remain as overrides (highest precedence: env > data/*.json > seed)
- settings.ts loadSettings() already reads data/settings.json — extend pattern to other configs
- Admin UI settings page already writes data/settings.json — extend to other config files

title: C1: Capability token framework
description:
Tool access is currently binary — either the agent has the tool or doesn't. Hardcoded blocks (base/operator layer editing) can't be unlocked without code changes. Need graduated autonomy so operators can configure appropriate boundaries.

Source: Architecture discussion, Lobstar operational failures, PSM implications

Files: New src/capabilities/, src/types.ts, tool files

Capability tokens: identity.read, identity.write.runtime, identity.write.base, identity.write.operator, memory.write, memory.delete, external.discord, external.email, external.web, git.read, git.write, lifecycle.restart, lifecycle.rebuild, repl.execute, shard.spawn

Tiers with default token sets:
- Nursery: Read all prompts. Write runtime/channel/task only. Memory write (no delete). No external actions. Think with tight limits. No self-restart. No git write.
- Apprentice: Write all prompts (with versioning). Memory write + soft delete. External via confirmation queue. Higher think limits. Shard spawn basic. Git read.
- Autonomous: Everything unlocked. External actions fire immediately. Full shard/git/identity. Self-restart/rebuild.
- Custom: Operator cherry-picks per-capability.

Design:
- Tier set via CAPABILITY_TIER env var or admin GUI
- Every tool checks required capability token at invocation time (not registration time)
- Tools always VISIBLE in tool list (she knows what she could do) but gated at execution
- Denied invocations return explanatory message, not silent failure
- Config: capability-tier.json — operator-editable, hot-reloadable via admin GUI

Acceptance:

title: Gateway split: voice turns need awaited agent response for TTS
description:
Voice runtime currently depends on `DiscordAdapter.onMessage()` returning the agent response synchronously so it can run TTS playback.

In gateway/agent split mode (`gateway-main.ts` + `agent-main.ts`), the gateway Discord handler forwards message notifications to agent via `gateway.notifyAll('discord.message', ...)` and returns a placeholder response immediately. This means voice transcript turns can produce empty responses at the adapter layer and skip TTS.

Why it matters:
- Single-process mode voice works with direct handler response.
- Split mode is the intended secure deployment model (keys host-side), so voice needs a request/response path there too.

Proposed fix directions:
1. Add a request-response RPC path for Discord turns (gateway asks one connected agent for response payload and waits with timeout), OR
2. Add dedicated voice reply RPC (`discord.voice.reply`) from agent to gateway carrying text/audio-ready payload tied to voice session, OR
3. Route voice turn through an explicit gateway event channel with correlation IDs and awaited reply.

Any solution must preserve existing text behavior and avoid double-send.
acceptance_criteria:
- In gateway+agent split mode, a voice transcript turn receives agent response and plays TTS
- No placeholder/empty response path in voice flow
- Text channel behavior remains unchanged
- Added integration test covering gateway+agent voice response correlation
close_reason: Implemented bidirectional JSON-RPC: JSONRPCServerAndClient per connection, discord.handleMessage reverse RPC, voice handler in adapter, gateway-main wiring, agent-main handler. 797 tests passing.

title: RLM loop lacks per-iteration LLM timeout/abort guard
description:
Summary:
RLM budget checks happen after each iteration, but the core LLM completion call inside the loop has no per-iteration timeout/abort wrapper. A stalled provider call can hang beyond think wall-time policy.

Why this is a bug:
- Budget and wall-time policy are intended safety bounds for autonomous loops.
- Without call-level timeout, loop control cannot enforce those bounds under provider stalls/network hangs.

Files to modify:
- src/repl/loop.ts
- src/repl/tools.ts (if surface message needs explicit timeout reason)
- src/repl/*.test.ts

Implementation steps:
1. Wrap each llmProvider.complete(...) call with timeout/abort behavior tied to remaining wall-time budget.
2. Return deterministic budget stop reason (e.g., llm timeout) when hit.
3. Ensure timeout path records partial trace/steps cleanly without crashing loop state.
4. Add regression tests using a slow/fake provider to verify bounded termination.

Example:
Before: provider stalls for minutes despite thinkMaxWallTimeMs=60000.
After: iteration aborts when budget is exceeded and loop exits with explicit stop reason.
acceptance_criteria:
- Think wall-time policy is enforced even when provider stalls
- Timeout exits are surfaced in ThinkResult with clear budget reason
- Tests cover hanging provider scenario
close_reason: Implemented and validated via focused module tests + build

- ModelPurpose includes reasoning, but runtime call paths do not expose or use it for think cycles.
- This breaks expected behavior when reasoning-capable models are configured separately from extraction models.

Implementation steps:

2. Route think-loop LLM calls to reasoning purpose/slot instead of extraction.
3. Ensure gateway protocol supports the new purpose end-to-end.
4. Preserve fallback behavior (reasoning -> chat if not explicitly configured) consistent with resolveModel() semantics.
5. Add tests verifying reasoning slot is used for think calls when configured.

Example:

After: think tool uses reasoning roster slot (or chat fallback), independent of extraction model.

title: Multi-model chat room: persistent model personas with isolated memory
description:
Summary:
Implement a multi-model chat room where PSFN can converse with multiple external model personas (for example Claude Opus 3) as peers, not as consensus variants. Each persona must retain its own conversation memory and run in an isolated context that is visible in the room but not merged into global system memory.

Why:
Current behavior supports direct user relay and MoA-style orchestration, but not persistent peer-to-peer model social chat within PSFN's own substrate.

1. Add a room participant model with explicit identity (`participantId`, provider/model, display name, enabled flag) and persisted settings storage.
2. Introduce a chat-room orchestrator path that routes turns between PSFN and selected participant personas without MoA consensus aggregation.
3. Persist per-participant conversation state in isolated memory namespaces so each persona keeps its own history while room transcript remains queryable.
4. Expose minimal admin API surface to create/list/update participants and start/resume room sessions using existing admin chat endpoints (full UX redesign can layer later).
5. Ensure participant responses are tagged in stream events so the UI can render speaker identity reliably.
6. Add regression tests for routing correctness, persona-memory isolation, and restart persistence of room/participant config.

Example (before -> after):
Before: PSFN can only chat with user relay or MoA variant routing; no persistent peer persona threads.
After: `room-1` includes `psfn` + `claude-opus-3`; both exchange turns, and `claude-opus-3` retains its own prior room memory across sessions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Room sessions can be created and resumed with 2+ model participants.
- Participant identity is visible in streamed events and persisted transcripts.
- Persona memory remains isolated per participant and is not mixed into unrelated global memory threads.
- Settings for participants survive process restart.

title: RLM+REPL Sandbox — context-as-object, programmatic memory access, sub-LM calls, self-modification
description:
Port the RLM (Recursive Language Model) paradigm into PSFN. Core insight: context is an object PSFN can programmatically inspect/query/transform, not tokens stuffed into a prompt. She decides what context she needs.

Reference: https://github.com/alexzhang13/rlm, https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24601

**Foundation:** pi-agent-core's `Agent` class is the base layer. PSFN already depends on `@mariozechner/pi-ai`; pi-agent-core (1,495 LoC, MIT, single dep) provides the agent loop with streaming events, steering, follow-ups, and declaration-merging extensibility. Build RLM on top of this, don't reimplement.

**What RLM adds on top of pi-agent-core:**
1. REPL sandbox — persistent code execution environment (TypeScript). Model writes ```repl blocks, system executes them, returns truncated output.
2. Context-as-object — memories (SQLite L2), sessions (pi JSONL), identity, modules exposed as queryable interfaces in REPL namespace.
3. Sub-LM calls — `llm_query()` / `llm_query_batched()` in REPL, routes through LLMProvider / pi-agent-core's streamFn. Delegate to cheaper models for bulk work.
4. Modified termination — `FINAL()` / `FINAL_VAR()` signals completion.
5. Self-modification — write/test/install modules at runtime via REPL.

**Recommended approach:** Dual-mode agent loop via pi-agent-core's Agent. Conversational mode (standard pi agent loop for chat) + cognitive mode (RLM-style for complex reasoning). Mode triggered by model request, event type, or user directive.

**New files (~800 LoC per spec):**
- `src/repl/sandbox.ts` — REPL environment with restricted globals, persistent state
- `src/repl/context.ts` — Context object exposing memories, sessions, identity, modules
- `src/repl/sub-lm.ts` — llm_query/llm_query_batched routing through pi's streamFn
- Agent integration via pi-agent-core's Agent callbacks (transformContext, convertToLlm)

**Security:** Gateway/agent split with --network=none Docker already provides the security boundary.
design: Dual-mode AgentLoop: detect ```repl blocks vs standard tool calls in model output, dispatch accordingly. Preserves backward compatibility. RLM loop: prompt -> extract code blocks (regex) -> execute in sandbox -> check FINAL() -> append truncated output -> repeat. Sandbox uses node:vm or similar restricted execution. Context objects are lazy-loaded interfaces (don't materialize full DB into memory). Sub-LM calls reuse existing LLMProvider interface.
close_reason: Implemented RLM+REPL sandbox: types, parser, vm sandbox, RLM iteration loop, think tool. 476 LoC production + 503 LoC tests. All 137 tests pass, clean build.

title: Cross-channel session mirroring (Telegram + Discord)
description:

Hermes reference: /gateway/mirror.py — when a message is delivered to another platform (cross-platform send, cron job), mirror_to_session appends a record to the receiving session's transcript. The agent sees these mirrored entries in its conversation history.

- When PSFN sends a response on channel A, check if the user has active sessions on other channels (B, C)
- Append a mirrored entry to those sessions: [Mirrored from #discord-general] PSFN: "..."
- Use a distinct message type (AgentMessage custom type 'mirror') so it can be filtered/styled differently
- Respect channel visibility rules — only mirror between channels that share continuity (private↔private per existing channelsShareContinuity())
- Include both agent responses AND user messages (bidirectional awareness)
- Mirror entries should be lightweight — maybe truncated to first N chars with a reference marker
- convertToLlm() should render mirrors as compact system notes, not full messages (avoid context bloat)

Privacy consideration: Trust-gated — don't mirror intimate/confidential content to lower-trust channels. Use existing evaluateMemoryPolicy() logic.

- Discord ↔ Telegram (primary use case)

title: Prompt stack v1: layered, editable, versioned prompts

5. Task overlays (reflection, planning, maintenance, recovery)

Implementation details:
- Add `src/identity/prompt-stack.ts` (or equivalent) with deterministic compose order and explicit precedence.
- Store layers in versioned files under `identity/prompts/` with metadata (id, layerType, enabled, priority, updatedAt, updatedBy, checksum).
- Keep runtime composition deterministic and pure: same inputs -> same composed prompt hash.
- Thread composed prompt into AgentLoop per turn (or cached with invalidation) so channel/task overlays can vary by context.
- Preserve existing trust adaptation in AgentLoop as either:
  a) dedicated trust overlay layer, or
  b) post-compose append step with explicit ordering contract.

- Add inline diff preview + rollback to previous version.

Safety constraints:
- No silent overwrite of base identity layer.
- Failed layer parse/validation must fail closed to last-known-good composed prompt.
- Every composition run emits structured diagnostics (active layers + hash) for debugging.
design:
Suggested shape:
- `PromptLayerStore` (filesystem-backed, versioned markdown/json metadata)
- `PromptComposer.compose({channelType, channelId, trustLevel, taskKind})`
- `PromptCache` keyed by context signature + layer set hash

Migration plan:
1) Lift current `composeSystemPrompt(card)` output into base layer adapter.
2) Add operator/runtime layers without behavior changes.
3) Introduce channel/task overlays incrementally (voice/heartbeat first).
acceptance_criteria:
- At least 5 layer classes supported: base/operator/runtime/channel/task.
- Composition order and precedence are deterministic and tested.

title: Adopt pi-agent-core as foundation runtime
description: Replace our custom AgentLoop (~253 LoC) with @mariozechner/pi-agent-core (~1,518 LoC) as the foundation agent runtime. pi-agent-core provides: double-loop pattern (tool+steering inner, follow-up outer), structured AgentEvent lifecycle (9 event types), AbortController propagation, steering/follow-up queues, TypeBox tool validation, structured tool results with toolCallId, custom message types via declaration merging, two-phase context transform (transformContext → convertToLlm). We already depend on pi-ai; agent-core is the same author, MIT, single dependency.
design:
Migration path (6 phases):
1. Add pi-agent-core dependency, create adapter layer mapping our interfaces
2. Migrate SubstrateTool → AgentTool (all tools get toolCallId, AbortSignal, onUpdate)
3. Adopt AgentMessage types + convertToLlm pipeline (session format change)
4. Replace streamWithToolLoop with agentLoop() + custom streamFn
5. Bridge AgentEvent → our EventBus (admin GUI, Discord adapter consume events)
6. Add steering/follow-up support to Discord adapter + API

Key constraint: single-process mode (npm run dev) must continue working. Gateway/agent split uses LLMProvider interface which maps to streamFn.
acceptance_criteria:
- pi-agent-core is a dependency in package.json
- Agent class wraps our LLM/memory/session stack
- All existing tools work via AgentTool interface
- Structured tool results with toolCallId (no more string concatenation)
- AbortController propagation (abort() cancels streaming + tools)
- Fine-grained events emitted (turn_start/end, tool_execution_start/end)
- Steering queue enables mid-run message injection
- All 500+ tests pass
- Single-process and gateway/agent modes both work
close_reason: All 6 subtasks complete. pi-agent-core adopted: SubstrateAgent wraps Agent, native AgentTool, AgentMessage+convertToLlm pipeline, event bridge, steering+follow-up queues, AbortController. 679 tests pass.

title: Controlled rejoin recovery after DAVE decrypt failures
description:
Implement automatic rejoin recovery when repeated DAVE decryption failures are detected. Currently, if DAVE decrypt fails, inbound audio is silently lost with no recovery mechanism — the connection stays "alive" but useless.

OpenClaw fix: "trigger controlled rejoin recovery after repeated decrypt failures to improve inbound STT stability under DAVE receive errors."

Design:
- Track decrypt failure count per connection (detect via opus decode errors, empty/garbled PCM, or @snazzah/davey error events)
- When failure count exceeds decryptionFailureTolerance threshold:
  1. Log warning with failure count
  2. Emit voice.connection.recovery event
  3. Leave current channel (full teardown)
  4. Wait brief cooldown (1-2s)
  5. Rejoin same channel (fresh DAVE handshake)
  6. Reset failure counter
- Limit rejoin attempts per time window to prevent rejoin storms (max 3 rejoins per 5 minutes)
- After max rejoins exhausted, emit error and stay disconnected (notify operator if ntfy configured)

Integration:
- Depends on DAVE config (PSFN-xxx) for tolerance threshold
- Depends on connection state monitoring (PSFN-xxx) for clean teardown/rejoin

title: Minimal Scheduler (MVP) — heartbeat, cron, one-shot, memory maintenance
description: Build the scheduler layer (~400 LoC) per spec Layer 6. Heartbeat timer (default 30min), cron/every/one-shot task registry, memory maintenance hooks. design: Files: src/scheduler/types.ts, src/scheduler/scheduler.ts, src/scheduler/heartbeat.ts. Memory maintenance (salience decay) already exists as SalienceDecay — register it as a scheduler task. Wire into runtime.ts + index.ts.

close_reason: Scheduler MVP implemented: types (TaskType, TaskState, ScheduledTask, SchedulerConfig), Scheduler class (register/unregister/start/stop/tick, heartbeat as special task), 17 unit tests, wired into runtime.ts (salience decay + heartbeat as scheduler tasks, Discord hourly heartbeat via DISCORD_HEARTBEAT_CHANNEL env), wired into agent-main.ts. 166 total tests passing.

title: SalienceDecay: wrap decay loop in db.transaction()
description:
decay.ts:27-48 runs individual UPDATE statements for each memory during salience decay. Each UPDATE is an implicit transaction with its own fsync. With 300 active memories, this means 300 fsyncs instead of 1.

title: Channel adapter decomposition — composable interface for multi-channel support
description:
Decompose the monolithic channel adapters (currently Discord is one big class, API is a single server file) into composable adapter interfaces inspired by OpenClaw's ChannelPlugin pattern. This prepares for adding Telegram and future channels without god objects.

OpenClaw decomposes channels into ~15 adapter facets. We don't need all of them — adopt the subset that matters for PSFN:

Core adapters (required):
- ChannelConfig — account/connection config
- ChannelOutbound — send text/media
- ChannelGateway — start/stop lifecycle

Optional adapters:
- ChannelSecurity — allowlists, DM policy
- ChannelStreaming — typing indicators, chunk coalescing
- ChannelThreading — reply-to, thread management
- ChannelPrompt — per-channel prompt hints (replaces resolveChannelType())
- ChannelCapabilities — feature flags (reactions, threads, media, etc.)

Also adopt the lightweight "dock" pattern: a minimal subset type for shared code paths that don't need heavy imports.

NOT adopting: full plugin registry, plugin manifests, multi-account per channel (unnecessary complexity for PSFN's single-agent model).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] ChannelAdapter interface with composable adapter facets
- [ ] ChannelCapabilities type with feature flags
- [ ] ChannelOutbound/Gateway/Config/Security/Streaming/Prompt adapter interfaces
- [ ] Discord adapter refactored to implement ChannelAdapter
- [ ] API server refactored to implement ChannelAdapter
- [ ] Channel registry (Map) in runtime for lookup by ID
- [ ] resolveChannelType() replaced by ChannelPromptAdapter
- [ ] Tests for adapter interface compliance

title: Improve LLM call observability and long-running turn UX (think/repl heavy flows)
description:
Summary:
Runtime INFO logs currently show many `ModelFallback` and `LLM complete finished` entries but do not include enough origin metadata to explain *what kind of call* they represent (chat vs tool vs memory vs summary vs compaction/deliberation) or which tool initiated them. This makes heavy think/repl sequences look opaque and can appear like runaway calls. Also, long-running turn handling does not provide a generic in-channel conversational status update ("still working") while processing, so users perceive silence/lockup.

Validated findings:
- `LLM complete finished` logs include purpose/model/provider/attempts, but no `channelId`, `turnId`, `origin`, `toolName`, or `toolCallId` (`src/llm/client.ts`).
- Fallback logs similarly omit execution origin metadata (`src/llm/fallback.ts`).
- Think/repl loop intentionally performs repeated `complete(..., "reasoning")` calls per iteration (`src/repl/loop.ts`) and sandbox `llm_query*` also calls reasoning complete (`src/repl/sandbox-capabilities/llm.ts`).
- Current REPL guardrails exist, but still allow many calls in autonomous tier: maxIterations 15, maxSubQueries clamped by runtime setting/tier, maxToolCalls 50 (`src/repl/types.ts`, `src/repl/loop.ts`, `src/repl/loop-helpers.ts`).
- Current runtime setting in this environment is `thinkMaxSubQueries=7` (`data/settings.json`), but iteration-level calls can still be high.
- Discord has compaction/retry status messages and steering on contention, but no generic long-running think status stream (`src/channels/discord/adapter.ts`). Telegram currently drops concurrent messages while busy (`src/channels/telegram/adapter.ts`).

Files to modify:
- src/llm/client.ts
- src/llm/fallback.ts
- src/agent/contracts.ts (or equivalent request metadata interface)
- src/repl/loop.ts
- src/repl/sandbox-capabilities/llm.ts
- src/session/manager/compaction-service.ts
- src/llm/deliberation.ts
- src/channels/discord/adapter.ts
- src/channels/telegram/adapter.ts
- optionally src/event-bus.ts + status emitter/wiring

Implementation steps:
1. Add structured request metadata for all LLM calls: `originType`, `originStage`, `channelId`, `turnId`, `toolName`, `toolCallId`, `requestId`.
2. Propagate metadata from major call sites (chat stream, think iteration, think subquery, memory/session summary, compaction, deliberation).
3. Extend INFO logs in LLM client/fallback to include this metadata and normalize one-line call classification fields.
4. Add long-running turn status behavior:
   - emit periodic progress/status events for think/repl loops (start, heartbeat, completed/aborted)
   - channel adapters send lightweight interim message/typing status (e.g. "still working") without breaking final response flow.
5. Ensure status updates are rate-limited/debounced and safely cleaned up on completion/error.
6. Add tests for metadata propagation and long-running status behavior across Discord/Telegram (or channel-agnostic event tests + adapter tests).

Acceptance criteria:
- From logs alone, operators can identify each LLM call class and originating tool/flow.
- Heavy think runs are visibly in progress to users (not silent waiting).
- No regression in existing retry/compaction status handling.
- REPL limit behavior remains enforced and visible in status/reporting.

comments.author: operator
comments.text: Additional requirement: long-running work must not block normal companionship/chat. Runtime should support concurrent background execution (plan/act loops, scheduled tasks, audits/subagent-style delegated jobs) while the primary chat channel remains responsive for ordinary conversation. Include explicit design for concurrent job orchestration, status reporting, cancellation, and channel-safe context separation.

title: Agent scratchpad memory
description:
Add a bounded, agent-managed scratchpad for deliberate note-taking alongside L2 contextual memories.

Rationale: L2 memories are subconscious — extracted by LLM, surfaced by embedding similarity. Scratchpad is deliberate — "V wants X done this way", "current project state", "tried Y, didn't work". Different cognitive function. Currently she can journal during heartbeat idle time, but has no active working-memory for ongoing tasks.

Design:
- ScratchpadStore: SQLite table or simple file-backed store

4. CLAUDE.md: Update test count, file count, LoC count to current state.
